- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp downward trend, reduce the forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is rising, cap the upward movement to prevent overshoot.  
- After a recent price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast to allow for a slight lagged rebound.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3 or more), reduce forecast volatility and favor smoother transitions.  
- If forecast mean is consistently above true mean over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction by 0.5–1.5% per day.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows mean reversion toward 65–70 range after 10+ days of high prices, model should be nudged toward that zone.  
- If sentiment history shows recent negative sentiment (last 3 days ≤0.3), forecast should be slightly conservative — avoid aggressive upward moves.
